title: Exact Values & Life Near a Wall

steps.body: Tangent's exact values come straight from the ratio of the exact sin/cos values you know: tan(π/6) = (1/2)/(√3/2) = **1/√3 ≈ 0.58**, tan(π/4) = 1, tan(π/3) = (√3/2)/(1/2) = **√3 ≈ 1.73**. The trio 0.58, 1, 1.73 climbs — as every tangent branch does.

predict.prompt: Walking the tangent trace toward 90°: what does the wave do?

options.label: It climbs without limit — there's a wall at 90°, not a value
It peaks at 1 and comes back down, like sine

predict.reveal: A wall. tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, and at 90° the denominator hits zero — the trace shoots off the top of the stage and reappears from the bottom. The zeros live where SINE is zero: at 0°, 180°, 360°. Drag past the wall and land on the crossing at 180°.

widget.prompt: Trace y = tan x: ride the branch up its wall at 90°, cross the gap, and land the tip exactly on the zero at 180°.
widget.successFeedback: Zero at 180° — sin 180° = 0 puts the ratio at 0/(−1) = 0. Between here and the wall the ratio ran through every value once, which is why tan(60°) = (√3/2)÷(1/2) = 1.73 exists on this branch: the entry above is one stop on the climb you just made.
widget.lowFeedback: Not at the zero — the tip is off the axis here. The crossing sits where the SINE leg vanishes; keep dragging toward 180°, through the wall's gap.
widget.highFeedback: Past the zero — the trace has started its next climb. Back up to 180°, where the wave touches the axis between two walls.

explanationVariants: π/6 and π/3 swap sine and cosine, so their tangents are reciprocals: 1/1.73 ≈ 0.58.

commonErrors.feedback: 1.73 is tan(π/3). At π/6 the SMALL value (1/2) is on top: 1/√3 ≈ 0.58.
0.5 is sin(π/6) before dividing. The quotient is (1/2)/(√3/2) ≈ 0.58.

steps.body: Pressed against a wall, tangent is one-sided: approaching π/2 **from the left**, cos shrinks through tiny POSITIVE values while sin ≈ 1, so tan → **+∞**; from the right, cos is tiny and NEGATIVE, so tan → **−∞**. Each branch exits its wall at opposite infinities.

explanationVariants: Just left of π/2 ≈ 1.5708, e.g. x = 1.55: sin ≈ 1 over cos ≈ +0.0208 gives roughly +48 — huge and positive.
Dividing nearly-1 by a shrinking positive number explodes upward.

widget.prompt: x = 1.55 sits just LEFT of the wall at π/2 ≈ 1.5708. tan(1.55) is approximately:

options.label: +48 — large and positive
options.feedback: Right — sin(1.55) ≈ 1.0 over cos(1.55) ≈ +0.021: the left side of a wall rockets up.

options.label: −48 — large and negative
options.feedback: Negative blow-up happens on the RIGHT of the wall (cos < 0 there). Left side: positive, ≈ +48.

options.label: about 1
options.feedback: tan = 1 back at π/4 ≈ 0.79. This close to the wall, cos ≈ 0.021 makes the quotient huge: ≈ 48.

explanationVariants: In Quadrant II (like 2.5 rad), sin > 0 and cos < 0: tangent is NEGATIVE — e.g. tan(3π/4) = −1.
Between the wall π/2 and the zero π, the branch is climbing from −∞ up to 0: all negative.

options.feedback: Right — sin(3π/4) = √2/2, cos(3π/4) = −√2/2: equal sizes, opposite signs → −1.
That's Quadrant I (π/4). In Quadrant II cosine has gone negative: tan(3π/4) = −1.

options.label: undefined
options.feedback: cos(3π/4) = −√2/2 ≠ 0 — no wall here. The value is −1.

explanationVariants: On one branch tangent strictly climbs: tan(1.0) ≈ 1.56 < tan(1.3) ≈ 3.60 < tan(1.5) ≈ 14.1 — the value closest to the wall is largest: x = 1.5.
All three x's sit left of π/2; nearer the wall means a smaller cosine below, a bigger quotient.
hints: All of 1.0, 1.3, 1.5 lie on the same branch (left of π/2).
Which x is closest to the wall at π/2 ≈ 1.5708?

widget.prompt: Among x = 1.0, 1.3, and 1.5, where is tan x LARGEST?

options.label: x = 1.5
options.feedback: Right — same branch, strictly climbing, and 1.5 presses closest to the wall (tan ≈ 14).

options.label: x = 1.0
options.feedback: tan(1.0) ≈ 1.6 — the branch keeps climbing past it. The wall-hugger 1.5 wins (≈ 14).

options.label: They're equal — tangent is periodic
options.feedback: Periodic across branches, but WITHIN one branch it strictly increases: 1.5, nearest the wall, is largest.

takeaways: tan(π/6), tan(π/4), tan(π/3) = 0.58, 1, 1.73 — from the sin/cos ratios.
Left of a wall: +∞; right of it: −∞.
Within a branch, tangent strictly increases.
steps.teaser: Next: stretching and squeezing the whole ladder — tangent transformations.

concept.body: To evaluate tangent exactly, divide the exact sine by the exact cosine — and read the SIGN from the quadrant (sin's sign over cos's sign).

explanationVariants: tan(π/4 + π) = tan(π/4) = 1 by the period — or directly: both coordinates −√2/2, ratio +1.

widget.prompt: Using sin(5π/4) = −√2/2 and cos(5π/4) = −√2/2, what is tan(5π/4)?

commonErrors.feedback: Two negatives divide to a POSITIVE: (−√2/2)/(−√2/2) = +1.
0.71 is √2/2, one coordinate. The quotient of the equal pair is 1.
